coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist, so the riskiest logic — sorting comparators, URL state, ref-to-species mapping, the fetch semaphore — has zero coverage; scoring on what would be caught, which is nothing.

evidence: app/src — no *.test.* or *.spec.* files; grep for test/assert/expect across app/src returns nothing
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: No tests at all, so the criterion bottoms out at 1 by definition.

evidence: app/src/lib/server/api.js:24 — global fetch with module-level cache: any data-layer refactor breaks silently
app/src/lib/server/data.js:61 — augment?.(ref, index, entry) positional coupling with app/src/routes/abilities/[name]/+page.server.js:18 (entries[index].is_hidden): refactor-safe only by luck
regression_power.rationale: Breaking any behaviour — sort order, hidden-ability flags, pagination clamping — would pass CI because there is no CI inside app/; the acceptance suite is external and won't be run by the owning team after refactor.

evidence: app/package.json:11-16 — devDependencies contain only the build toolchain; no test infra to evaluate
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, per the rubric's anchor for the no-tests case.

findings.issue: Zero tests of any kind: no test script, no runner dependency, no test files in 22 source files.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest + @testing-library/svelte or Playwright component tests; at minimum unit-test lib/utils.js and the two comparators, which are pure and trivially testable.

findings.issue: augment(ref, index, entry) passes the ref's index, and the abilities route (app/src/routes/abilities/[name]/+page.server.js:15-18) re-indexes into a different array (entries) assuming positional alignment; any filtering/reordering in speciesFromPokemonRefs silently attaches hidden-ability flags to the wrong Pokémon.
findings.suggestion: Pass the raw entry through to augment instead of an index, and pin the behaviour with a test using a Pokémon that has both a normal and a hidden entry.

findings.issue: The sort comparator encodes three spec rules at once (missing-values-last in both directions, number vs string compare, tiebreak order) and is the only place the default Level-Up-by-level ordering is enforced; no test can fail if any of it breaks.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator to a pure module and unit-test: null handling in both directions, stable tiebreak, aria-sort state transitions.

findings.issue: URL state parsing (page clamping, NaN/garbage page, invalid type/generation values falling through to zero results) is untested; these are precisely the inputs users and crawlers will send.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test load() with a stubbed fetch for page=abc, page=99999, ?type=notatype, and filter-reset-to-page-1 transitions.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled semaphore (inflight/waiters with shift) plus a never-invalidating module-level Map cache; a deadlock or over-fetch regression only manifests under real concurrency, and no test exercises either.
findings.suggestion: Test with >MAX_CONCURRENT parallel fetches asserting all resolve, and make the cache injectable/inspectable so tests can assert hits vs misses.

findings.issue: The method-order comparator uses sentinel indexOf arithmetic for 'Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor, then others alphabetically' — dense logic, easy to break for unknown methods, completely unguarded.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with a fixture containing level-up, tutor and a hypothetical 'other' method, asserting exact table order.

findings.issue: Search UX correctness (typed override, 250 ms debounce, afterNavigate reset, race between a pending debounce and a select change) has no test; 'updates as the user types' is spec-required behaviour that a refactor of this component could silently break.
findings.suggestion: Add a Playwright test typing a query and asserting both the rendered results and the URL parameter, including typing then immediately changing a filter.

findings.issue: The data layer hard-wires api() (which reads process.env and global fetch at import time, api.js:6,24), so load functions and data.js cannot be unit-tested without module mocking — the structural reason no tests exist.
findings.suggestion: Inject the client (pass api as a parameter or use SvelteKit's fetch in load) so tests can stub responses without magic.

findings.issue: Only 404 is treated as a known outcome; API 500s/timeouts propagate as opaque errors with no test of what the user sees, and error() calls in +page.server.js:44 fire whole-list 500s on a single missing record.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that a single unavailable Pokémon record doesn't take down the whole home page.

findings.issue: Type labels use humanize(type.name) while the home page resolves English names from /type (+page.server.js:52) — an untested assumption that the two always coincide; a data change would produce wrong labels unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Route all type labels through one English-name resolver and test it.

summary: The app ships with no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no test files — leaving 648 LOC of data transformation, URL-state parsing, ref-to-species mapping and a dense client-side sort comparator entirely unguarded once the external acceptance suite stops being the safety net. The most refactor-fragile seam is the index-based augment coupling between speciesFromPokemonRefs and the abilities route, which would silently mislabel hidden abilities. The pure helpers in utils.js and both comparators would have been cheap, high-value unit tests; the fact that data.js can't be tested without mocking is the structural root cause and worth fixing.
